content.text: Section 24 fully addresses the rule at the preferred level, and no other clause creates an adverse change-of-control right.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full: 24.1 lets us assign without Vendor consent to an Affiliate or to a successor by merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets; 24.2 bars Vendor assignment (including transfer by change of control or delegation of material performance) without our prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld, and bars assignment to a direct competitor; 24.3 applies a reciprocal reasonable-consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 confirms our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, so the walk-away risks are absent. Section 13.3 is consistent, allowing licence rights to travel with a Section 24 assignment, and Section 9's insolvency trigger expressly excludes a lawful reorganization. One minor point short of ideal wording: the competitor bar in 24.2 is qualified by "without Customer's consent" rather than absolute, which we note but do not redline since it remains within our control.
